display_name: Read a session's gauge SERIES and what it means
description: GAU-15 (2026-08-19). Reads the bounded append-only series behind the single cached row session_context_status returns, newest first, and classifies what the series means. The cache is upsert-only -- one row per agent_instance_id, last write wins -- so before this table existed the readings on either side of a freeze were overwritten by the subject's own next write, and a /clear keeps the instance id, so one row silently spanned both sides of a rotation. That is why the original 85-minute gauge freeze of 2026-08-18 could never be analysed after the fact. Accepts EITHER id the session is known by (the ledger id the rows are keyed on, or the watch id peer_list publishes), resolved through the same peer-binding join as session_context_status, and reports which path it took in id_resolution. Each entry carries three clocks that answer three different questions: reading_at (when the reading itself was produced, from the transcript line whose usage block yielded the number; null means NOT REPORTED by that reporter, never 'same as measured_at'), measured_at (when the reporting hook observed it), and recorded_at (when the state layer stored it) -- so observation lag and delivery lag are both readable rather than assumed. series_state classifies the series against the lifecycle row's own last report_alive: 'healthy' (the series is moving), 'stopped' (the series stalled while report_alive kept landing -- the session works and its gauge is dark, which IS the GAU-01 class), 'idle' (both clocks stopped together, so nobody is driving the session; a normal fleet state and NOT an incident), 'never_started' (no series has ever been written), or 'undetermined' (something needed was unreadable, said plainly rather than guessed). series_state_reason gives the evidence in numbers. rotation_boundaries counts how many /clear splices the page spans, measured as changes of claude_session_id under one instance id, so a reader never mistakes a new context's reading for a movement in the old one. truncated is published rather than implied, because a reader asking when a gauge stopped is asking about the OLDEST row on the page. Retention is bounded by the writer itself at 64 rows per session, hard-deleted at write time -- no reaper, and no soft-delete flag that nothing ever clears.
embedding_description: Reading the history of a session's context-window readings rather than only the latest one, to tell whether its gauge stopped advancing while the session was still working, whether nobody was driving the session at all, and when a context rotation split the series in two.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: resolved, resolution_error, agent_instance_id (the ledger id the series is keyed on), queried_agent_instance_id, id_resolution, series_state, series_state_reason, last_report_alive, entries (newest first: recorded_at, measured_at, reading_at, current_tokens, ceiling, model, claude_session_id, agent_session_id, cache_read_tokens, cache_cold, cache_overage_signature, reporter_surface, reporter_generation), returned, truncated, retention, rotation_boundaries.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Lead with series_state and quote series_state_reason -- it carries the ages the classification used. Treat 'idle' as a normal state and do NOT report it as a fault; treat 'stopped' as the incident. When rotation_boundaries is greater than zero, say so before comparing the newest and oldest readings: they belong to different contexts and the step between them is a rotation, not a measurement. If truncated is true, say the series continues past this page rather than describing the oldest entry as the beginning. Never fill a null reading_at with measured_at -- that would report zero observation lag exactly where the lag is unknown.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: A 'stopped' verdict is the GAU-01 signature and warrants capturing the series before the session rotates. A 'never_started' verdict beside a recent last_report_alive points at the gauge reporter specifically; beside no report_alive at all it points at a session nobody has driven.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: One bounded ordered page over session_context_status_history plus one managed_session row read, both through the state interface.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: missing_argument: agent_instance_id was empty. state_service_unavailable: the state service is not bound. ambiguous_agent_session_id: more than one gauge row claims the same stable session id, so the watch-id join cannot say which session was meant. An absent series is NOT an error -- it returns resolved=false with series_state 'never_started' in a normal successful result.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For missing_argument, supply the target session's agent_instance_id (from list_sessions or session_status, or a session's own AGENT_INSTANCE_ID). For ambiguous_agent_session_id, inspect the named rows rather than retrying: two live sessions sharing one agent_session_id is stale or duplicate data to reconcile. For a series_state of 'undetermined', read series_state_reason -- it names which input was unreadable.
